rationale: A wins because it keeps the sharpest story as a testable thesis: "Toast tells investors hardware is low-margin — the real bet is lending to the same 120,000 restaurants" asks for filings, segment margins, and credit-cycle proof. B has real shapes, but it steps on a rake with "Toast got profitable by selling money, not hardware" — a causal claim the update does not give you. That is the difference between a reporter hook and a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: Angle overlap: "Toast tells investors hardware is low-margin" and "Vertical SaaS found its margin — and it's not the software" both lean on the same margin-mix thesis. One needs a cleaner public-markets lane, the other needs broader category evidence.
Grounding stretch: "opting out of its financial products comes with real friction" is plausible, but the update does not prove switching friction. It needs owner evidence before it becomes copy.

The payroll angle imports extra terrain: "tipped minimum wage variation by state, tip pooling rules, tip credits" may be true industry context, but it is not in the fact block. Keep it as required proof, not assumed product relevance.
The default-rate angle overstates with "That's the number that matters." For borrowers, effective cost and fees may matter more; default rates are the investor/regulator question.
gaps_in_B: Invented causality: "Toast got profitable by selling money, not hardware" is not in the update. The update says Toast reached profitability and says fintech is higher-margin; it does not say fintech caused profitability.

Unsupported foil: "Restaurants are borrowing from their point-of-sale system instead of their bank" and "positions the POS company against community banks" assume bank displacement the facts do not establish.

Unverified mechanics: "underwritten by the payment flow Toast already sees" is a smart inference, but it is still an inference. Do not present it as fact without Toast saying it or filings showing it.
The trend and markets angles both ride "fintech is higher-margin than hardware." They are distinct enough to keep, but they need different proof packages or they collapse into the same story twice.
